/-!
# Erdős Problem 1159

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1159](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1159)
- [ESS83] Erdős, P. and Silverman, R. and Stein, A., *Intersection properties of families containing
  sets of nearly the same size*. Ars Combin. (1983), 247--259.
- [Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
-/

open Configuration

namespace Erdos1159

/--
Determine whether there exists a constant $C>1$ such that the following holds.

Let $P$ be a finite [projective plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projective_plane). Must there exist a set of points $S$ such that $1\leq \lvert S\cap \ell\rvert \leq C$ for all lines $\ell$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_1159 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C : ℕ, 1 < C ∧
      ∀ (P L : Type) (_ : Membership P L) (_ : Fintype P) (_ : Fintype L),
        ∀ _ : ProjectivePlane P L, ∃ S : Set P, ∀ l : L,
          1 ≤ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ∧ (S ∩ {p : P | p ∈ l}).ncard ≤ C := by
  sorry

end Erdos1159

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly takes the universal upper-bound constant C in ℕ, whereas the source leaves its numerical domain implicit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Allowing a real constant C > 1 gives the same problem: choose a natural number N > C, uniformly for every plane, and every intersection bounded by C is also bounded by N. Conversely, a natural bound can be regarded as a real bound, preserving both inequalities. The full equivalence, including all plane and set quantifiers, was proved as Review1159.naturalBound_iff_realBound in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's projective-plane question. The constant is uniform across planes, and one set must satisfy the bounds on every line. Fintype P ensures all counted intersections are finite; Mathlib's ProjectivePlane excludes degenerate planes. Scratch checks compiled without errors or sorry-dependent proofs, verifying the nonempty-intersection interpretation, exclusion of empty and singleton witnesses, and a Fano-plane instance: C = 2 is impossible there, while C = 3 works. The source still records OPEN, with a last-edit date of 10 April 2026. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review; the reviewed file remains unchanged.
